# AI Trail — Badge Progression Reference

> Source: AI Trail SDLC Rollout Plan slides (official program documentation).
> Purpose: Planning reference for individual progress tracking system.

---

## Program Goals

The AI Trail framework exists to rapidly expand AI SDLC adoption across engineering through community, rewards, and a structured learning progression.

**Why the trail exists:**
- Multiply productivity through AI in the SDLC
- Encourage community growth around AI practices
- Create a clear pathway for rolling out new techniques

**Expected outcomes (Faster, More, Better, All):**
- **Faster**: Increased Epic/Feature Cycle Time
- **More**: Increased Total Epic/Feature Output
- **Better**: Reduced Epic to Work Order (WO) Ratio
- **All**: 100% of Engineers achieve Wayfinder badge

**Community structure:** Guilds of ~6 engineers meet weekly for knowledge sharing. AI Trail leadership facilitates a monthly meeting for all guilds.

---

## The Four Badges

| Badge | Description |
|---|---|
| **Greenhorn** | No prior experience. Learning the basics requires close guidance and guardrails. |
| **Wayfinder** | Familiar with the trail. Uses AI effectively without compromising quality, independently. |
| **Trail Guide** | Mastered the path. Coaches individuals and teams through known routes. |
| **Pioneer** | Explores unmapped territory. Establishes new techniques that may become future standards. |

---

## Badge 1 — Greenhorn

### Expectations
- GitHub Copilot (or equivalent) installed and working in Agent mode
- Complete AI-First SDLC training materials:
  - Introduction to AI-First SDLC
  - Lunch and Learn slide deck and recording
- Complete additional training covering:
  - Environment setup and spec-driven frameworks
  - Enhanced agent context setup (GitHub Copilot + VS Code)
  - Multi-repository workspace setup
  - AI Attribution practices
  - Context engineering best practices (reverse prompting, researching existing code, agent skills)
  - Quality control with AI (code reviews via ADO and GitHub, local code review, test case generation, WO troubleshooting)
  - Advanced topics (cloud agents, multiple agents, monitoring dashboards)

### Exit Criteria (evidence required to advance to Wayfinder)

| Criterion | Evidence Required |
|---|---|
| Deliver a sample application using GitHub Copilot + Agent OS | Feature branch pushed with your name in branch name; branch submitted for review |
| Complete AI-First SDLC Training | Proof of training completion |
| Deliver 5 stories using Agent Mode | Evidence of 5 completed stories |

**Completion reward:** Wayfinder Coin

---

## Badge 2 — Wayfinder

### Expectations
- Complete GitHub Copilot training (Course GH-300T00-A or equivalent)
- Delivery practices:
  - 80% of stories developed using AI tooling over 3 months
  - Configure agent instructions for your repositories (`copilot-instructions.md`, etc.)
  - Use AI to research Epics and WOs during grooming
  - Utilize Agent OS or a specification-driven development pattern
  - Understand and articulate context engineering to peers
- Participate in an AI guild with regular attendance; share learned techniques

### Exit Criteria (evidence required to advance to Trail Guide)

| Criterion | Evidence Required |
|---|---|
| Training | Proof of GitHub Copilot training completion |
| AI-assisted delivery | Evidence of ≥80% AI-tooling usage over 3 months, minimum 30 stories completed with AI |
| Repository configuration | GitHub links to repository agent instruction configuration |
| AI-assisted research | 3 Webex recordings of using AI to research a WO or new Epic |
| AI guild participation | Evidence of guild membership and regular attendance |

**Completion reward:** Claude Code License

---

## Badge 3 — Trail Guide

### Expectations
- SDLC:
  - Continue delivering ≥80% of code using AI Agents
  - Contribute to AI SDLC best practices (documentation, shared context, shared tooling)
  - Automate the SDLC for tech debt and work order items
- Multi-Agent Development:
  - Configure local development to support multiple concurrent agents
  - Use multi-agent handoff: decompose an Epic into spec, then have sub-agents work individual stories
- Lead an AI Guild:
  - Start and lead a guild of at least 5 engineers
  - Meet weekly; facilitate growth in the AI SDLC

### Exit Criteria (evidence required to advance to Pioneer)

| Criterion | Evidence Required |
|---|---|
| Automated code delivery | Working agent-automated code delivery pipeline with human-in-the-loop code review |
| Multi-agent development | Evidence of using a multi-agent setup locally to deliver epics |
| Lead a guild | Recruit a guild of ≥5 engineers; coach 5 engineers to achieve Trail Guide badge |

**Completion reward:** Pioneer Hoodie

---

## Badge 4 — Pioneer

### Expectations
- Pilot new tooling and practices:
  - Bring new tools and approaches to AI Trail leadership for review
  - Run pilots to help determine viability
- AI SDLC thought leadership:
  - Monthly: create and publish articles for the engineering group on AI engineering practices
  - Collaborate with Product, UX, and PMO to improve/accelerate AI utilization across the full SDLC
- Lead the AI Trail:
  - Create and present content for the monthly AI Trail meeting
- Continue meeting all expectations from previous badges

### Exit Criteria

No formal exit criteria defined (terminal badge). Evidence focus is on ongoing contribution and community impact.

---

## Tracking System Planning Notes

The following dimensions should be tracked per engineer:

- **Current badge** and **target badge**
- **Criterion status per badge**: not started / in progress / evidence submitted / approved
- **Evidence links**: branch URLs, training certificates, Webex recording links, guild attendance logs, repo config links
- **Reviewer/approver decisions** per criterion with comments and timestamps
- **Promotion history**: immutable record of badge changes with approver and rationale
- **Guild membership**: guild name, join date, attendance evidence

Key validation rules to enforce in the tracking system:
- Promotion to next badge requires all exit criteria approved
- Rejected or needs-update decisions must include a reviewer comment
- Level transitions are forward-only (rollback requires explicit reason and approver)
- Do not store PII or credentials in evidence fields — use links to controlled systems
